create.name: Trudy Goodman
create.bio:
Trudy Goodman is a Buddhist meditation teacher in the Theravada Insight (Vipassana) tradition, based in Los Angeles, where she founded the meditation centre InsightLA. Her own practice goes back to the mid-1970s, first in Zen and later in Insight meditation, and through the 1990s she taught Zen at the Cambridge Buddhist Association in Massachusetts. Before teaching full time she trained in developmental psychology at Harvard and worked for many years as a psychotherapist, and she was among the earliest instructors of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction, teaching it alongside Jon Kabat-Zinn in the early 1980s. She was also a co-founder of a Cambridge institute that brings meditation and psychotherapy together.

InsightLA began in 2002 with a handful of students and grew into a centre offering Buddhist teachings alongside secular mindfulness and compassion courses, with sites in Santa Monica and Benedict Canyon and a large online community. Trudy leads retreats, weekend programmes and Sunday talks there and at other centres, often teaching with her husband, Jack Kornfield, and her recorded talks and guided meditations are freely available online. She has contributed chapters to several books on mindfulness and psychotherapy, and some viewers know her voice from the animated series The Midnight Gospel.

courses.title: The Seven Factors of Awakening
courses.description: A residential retreat at Big Bear Retreat Center in the California mountains, co-taught with Lisa Ernst and Catherine Shaddix. Through sitting and walking practice, talks and small-group meetings it explores the Buddha's seven qualities that support awakening, from mindfulness and joy to calm and equanimity.

courses.title: Deepening the Path: A Yearlong Program for Experienced Practitioners (2027)
courses.description: A year-long cohort programme at InsightLA for experienced meditators, combining practice and Buddhist study over six weekends at its Benedict Canyon house (non-residential), with an online option. Trudy teaches with Jack Kornfield and a group of other senior Insight teachers.

flags: Own site trudygoodman.com found via a web search for the domain name (it appeared in search results and the search summary); the site is clearly hers. Its contact page has a form block that says it is not set up, so no contact form URL recorded.
No Esalen mention on her own site (home, about, contact, offerings, audio pages): listed without the link.

Her offerings page names the Insight Meditation Society only as part of the 'Insight LA, Spirit Rock and IMS community' of senior teachers for the 2027 Deepening the Path programme; not added as a hub link because it does not say she has taught at IMS. Owner may decide.
Base: Los Angeles, from her InsightLA author bio ('lives in Los Angeles') and her own about page (she moved to Los Angeles and founded InsightLA).

She founded InsightLA, so its programme counts under the founder rule. Deepening the Path: her own site lists it as 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2027; InsightLA's page gives the first session as 23 Jan 2027 and the price as $1,950 (currency not stated beyond '$').
Seven Factors of Awakening: her site's 'register' link goes to a Big Bear Retreat Center URL containing '/2016/' (not opened), so her own event page is used as the URL; price not shown on her page.
Possible link to an existing listing: co-teacher Lisa Ernst already has a Spiritpedia plan (lisa-ernst.json). Her husband Jack Kornfield co-leads several items.
Her past career was psychotherapy, but her current work is Buddhist meditation teaching; the gut-health and chronic-pain videos in the playlist were left out.
Photos: three from her own site (black-and-white close-up, striped shirt, seated meditation), looked at; the third looks a good deal younger, but all come from her own site as her images.
left_out: Books: she is a contributing author only (chapters in Clinical Handbook of Mindfulness; Compassion and Wisdom in Psychotherapy; Mindfulness and Psychotherapy), not an author or co-author.

Life Blooms in the Midst of Suffering (Sangha Live short course) and Nourishing the Soul of Psychotherapy (2020 symposium): placeholder 2027 dates on an old item and a therapists' symposium; not clear they are current.
Sunday Sangha (1 Nov 2026), Halloween brunch fundraiser (31 Oct 2026), Transform Trauma Oxford (Sept 2026), BuddhaFest (July-Aug 2026): past; the trauma conference is also condition-named.
